analysis.method: Five warm-ups and ten timed samples in each process; two interleaved processes per implementation per round. Triggered rows repeat in reverse order. Regressions require the same threshold on both rounds. Spread is retained; no significance claim from a single median.
analysis.interpretation: Threshold triggers require source-path investigation and explicit acceptance for any deliberate cost before stable release. Performance alone does not establish independent fidelity, zero handoff copies or leak freedom.

findings: The 14 targeted comparisons with PR31 have no latency or RSS threshold trigger. Their observed latency deltas range from -4.94% to +3.67%; these small changes are not claimed as speedups. Default pixel/native output bytes match all 22 retained PR31 streams.

Against the predecessor, 21 paired rows retain >5% latency increases and four retain >5% RSS increases on both interleaved rounds. Every row, raw sample, spread and repeat is retained; no aggregate average hides these cases.

Separate three-second samples identify residual/predictor work and ANS refill-state counting as major Modular CPU work. VarDCT sampling is dominated by scaled transforms and hierarchical strategy analysis, with deadline checks also visible. These implementation files are byte-identical to PR31; profiling identifies optimisation targets without proving that one function explains the entire predecessor gap.

Allocating JPEG XL decode uses UInt16 storage in the successor; the predecessor uses UInt8 for 8-bit frames. Those 8-bit decode rows include the public output-layout migration cost. Both carry identical meaningful samples; the comparison does not isolate equal-storage kernels.

The 2048-square flat UInt16 lossless case grows from 363 to 367 bytes (+1.1019%). The retained source/bitstream investigation identifies the four-byte ANS terminal state for the empty global pixel stream. It is an explained encoding decision; stable acceptance has not been inferred.

The four RSS triggers remain measured process-level differences. Sampled heap endpoints and peak RSS cannot establish exact algorithm workspace or allocation/lifetime causes. No exact peak or leak-freedom claim is made.

The native preflight/timing hash-seed mismatch was reproduced twice, then corrected only in native baseline setup. Exact original-JPEG restoration and independent djxl restoration passed before the resumed native timings. The original failed attempt remains retained.

Natural progressive JPEG is rejected by both predecessor native and pixel paths with malformedACSymbol; those three timed rows are candidate-only. Eight pixel decode rows also lack an eligible predecessor. No speed ratio is assigned to excluded comparisons.
investigation.gateStatus: Investigation completed; predecessor performance/size acceptance remains open for stable release. No threshold waived and no production switch authorised.
